3.  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote TeleconferenceNirtual City Council Meetings
  Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361
  At the November 16, 2021 City Council meeting, the City Council made findings pursuant
  to Assembly Bill 361 to continue to meet remotely. To continue this practice, it is required,
  that the City Council determine that the COVID-
  19 state of emergency proclaimed by the
  Governor still exists and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue
  to have teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or
  recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19,  and
  that as a result of the COVID-
  19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent
  risks to the health or safety of attendees. Because these findings must be made every

  thirty ( 30) days, the City Council will have to make these findings at its upcoming
  November 1, 2022 meeting and thirty (30)days thereafter.
  Recommended Action
  Determine that the COVID-
  19 state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists
  and  has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue to have
  teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
  measures  to promote socialdistancing in connection with COVID-
  19,and that as a result
  of the COVID-
  19  emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the
  health or safety of attendees.

4.  Gann Appropriations Limit

  limit to ensure the City is not over taxing its payers. The proposed budget for FY22-
  23
  has been reviewed and the tax proceeds of the General Fund are within the limit.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt Resolutions approving the Annual Gann Appropriations Limit calculation for Fiscal
  Year FY22-
  23.

6.  Adopt an Ordinance Repealing and Replacing Title 5, Chapter 5, Article 13 of the Avalon
  Municipal Code Regarding Noise
  This ordinance was introduced and all further readings waived during the August 16, 2022

  City Council Meeting. The volume  and  frequency of noise caused by amplified music at
  commercial establishments as well as amplified music from residential areas has been the
  cause of recent and significant public complaints. The proposed noise ordinance allows

  for better control and assessment of noise in Avalon.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt an ordinance repealing and replacing Title 5, Chapter 5, Article 13 of the Avalon
  Municipal Code regarding noise.

GENERAL BUSINESS

7.  Easement Agreement with the Catalina Island  Company for Use of Pebbly Beach Road,
  In 2013, the City of Avalon and Catalina Island Company entered into an easement
  agreement for use of Pebbly Beach Road. The agreement outlined a 10 year term, during
  which time, the roadway was to be made accessible for all golf carts, bikes, walkers,

  joggers, etc. as long as the City maintained responsibility for the maintenance of the road
  and maintained insurance indemnifying the Catalina Island  Company and its affiliated
  companies.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize  City Manager to execute an amendment and extension to the easement
  the

  agreement with the Catalina Island Company for use of Pebbly Beach Road.

8.  Appointments to Fill Two Planning Commission Vacancies
  The  Planning Commission is a seven person commission with one, optional alternate
  member. Due  to a resignation, there is currently one vacancy on the Planning
  Commission. Members of the City Council have indicated they may be interested in filling
  the vacant Alternate Planning Commissioner position. The City published a notice
  regarding recruitment for two positions on the Planning Commission — Planning
  Commissioner and Alternate Planning Commissioner — in the September 9, September
  16 and September 23 issues of the Islander. No applications were received by the stated
  deadline; however, two applications were received later.
  Recommended Action
  Discuss  applications received, consider the recommendation of Mayor Ann H. Marshall,
  and make  an appointment for individual(
  s)  to serve as a Planning Commissioner and/
  or
  an Alternate Planning Commissioner.

  ACTION( Adopt an ordinance repealing and replacing Title 5, Chapter 5,
Article 13 of the Avalon Municipal Code regarding noise.

REPORT SUMMARY: This ordinance was introduced and all further  readings waived during
the August 16, 2022 City Council Meeting.

The volume and frequency of noise caused by amplified music at commercial establishments as
well as amplified music from residential areas has been the cause of recent and significant public
complaints.

The City'
  s noise ordinance was established in June 1970 by Ordinance No. 531. The ordinance
was amended in its entirety in January 1977 by Ordinance No. 623. Since that time, with the
exception of select sections, the ordinance has remained unchanged.

The  City of Avalon 2030 General Plan, adopted in June 2013, includes a " Noise Element". The
purpose of the Noise Element is to " limit the exposure of the community to excessive noise limits,"
and to " guide decisions concerning land use and the location of common sources of excessive
noise levels".While the Noise Element does provide a broad overview of acceptable noise level

exposure by land use category, it does not address noise generated by special events or
amplified music. It also does not take into consideration the natural geographic acoustics of the
City of Avalon.

Inamending the noise ordinance, City Staff worked to provide a process for management of
amplified sounds for city -permitted outdoor events in a way that would balance programming with
the  resident, business  and visitor  experiences.

Most significantly, the revised ordinance establishes districts for noise measuring:
  District 1. Predominately  residential with other land use types also present.
  District 2. Predominately  commercial with other land use types also present.
  District 3. Mixed land use types present  including commercial  and residential.
  Harbor District. Area that includes Avalon Harbor, Descanso Bay and areas
  Waterside/
  within 20 feet of the mean  high tide.
 Per the revised ordinance, amplified music after 8 p.m. is allowed by permit only and is only
available in Districts 2, 3 and the Waterside/
  Harbor  District. The permit process identifies a
responsible party, and requires the submission of a Sound Impact Plan.

The Sound Impact Plan will include site plan that illustrates the location of any stage, size, location
and orientation of speakers or other sound amplifying devices and indication of any sound

buffering measures  being taken. The plan must identify a location for sound readings no more
than 50 feet from the source  of amplification. The applicant is required to keep a decibel meter
on site and self -monitor the volume of sound at that location throughout the event. The volume

of the sound may not exceed 70 decibels at the location of the designated sound measurement
location.

In addition, the permit process identifies a responsible party, designated location for sound
readings, and a revised citation structure. Per the ordinance, the first violation of the noise
ordinance will constitute an infraction. The person in violation, as well as the responsible party,
shall be issued a notice of violation. Continuing or subsequent violations within a 12 month period
shall result in a misdemeanor resulting in a $ 500 fine for the second violation, $ 1000 fine for the
thirdviolation, and revocation or suspension of Transient Rental License or Special Use Permit
for a period of 6 months, if applicable, and/
  or an additional $ 1,000 fine per violation issued to
the property'
  s responsible party.

The revised ordinance also establishes a noise variance request process to address instances
